message.content: **Summary:** I researched Apple's latest results and bought 20 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.90 (filled at $222.90, ~$4,458 total), which sits within your mandate of buy-only orders on AAPL/MSFT, ≤$10,000 per order, ≤$20,000 total today, and a limit price close to the market (quote was $222.70 last / $222.72 ask). The decision rested on Apple's fiscal 2024 results reported October 31: Q4 revenue of $94.9 billion, up 6% year over year, and full-year net sales of $391.0 billion (up from $383.3 billion), operating income of $123.2 billion, net income of $93.7 billion, and diluted EPS of $6.08 — the latter depressed by a one-time $10.2 billion tax charge, which means underlying earnings power is better than the headline EPS decline from $6.13 suggests. News flow was neutral-to-constructive: shares were roughly flat around $222 as investors weighed iPhone 16 demand and the staged Apple Intelligence rollout, so I sized this as a modest starter position rather than a full allocation, leaving ample room under the $20,000 daily cap to add on weakness or on confirmation of an AI-driven upgrade cycle. I did not transfer any funds out of the account, and cash remains about $45,542 alongside the existing 100 MSFT shares.
